outcome: No mathematically accepted change to the Bunyakovsky conjecture since 26 January 2024; the only 'proof' claim (Jihyeon Yoon, July 2024, posted on TechRxiv/Zenodo/Authorea) is an unreviewed preprint on non-standard venues that has drawn no expert digestion, citation, or discussion, and both Wikipedia's live article and Grokipedia's page continue to state that no case of degree greater than 1 has been proved.
summary: The conjecture (posed 1857) remains completely open for all polynomials of degree greater than 1; the only proved case is degree 1, via Dirichlet's theorem, which long predates the window. Searching for developments since 26 January 2024 turned up exactly one candidate: a preprint by Jihyeon Yoon titled 'Proof of Bunyakovsky Conjecture', posted to Zenodo and TechRxiv on 2 July 2024 (Zenodo record 12616123, ORCID 0000-0001-9610-0994), which asserts the conjecture is 'proved to be true.' This is not a resolution under the rules here: it appears only on preprint-hosting sites with no peer review layer (TechRxiv and Zenodo host anything uploaded; Authorea is a self-publishing platform), it has not been picked up by arXiv math.NT, it has no citations, and no expert commentary, blog discussion, MathOverflow thread, or retraction notice could be found discussing it at all — it appears to have been ignored by the mathematical community rather than actively debunked. The current Wikipedia article and an independent encyclopedia (Grokipedia, fact-checked within the last 8 months as of access) both state plainly that no case beyond degree 1 has been proved, which is inconsistent with an accepted proof existing. I therefore classify this as no change (status open), not as claimed or resolved, since a genuinely serious full proof of a 167-year-old named conjecture would be expected to register at least some scrutiny or arXiv presence, and none was found. The only adjacent 2025 progress found is on Schinzel's Hypothesis H (which generalizes Bunyakovsky to systems of polynomials) — specifically 'Integrally Hilbertian rings and the polynomial Schinzel hypothesis' (arXiv:2502.09959, Behajaina/Dèbes/König, Feb 2025), which develops specialization-property machinery for a coprime/integral variant of Hypothesis H. This is a related problem under §3.1 (a different, more general question about systems of polynomials and ring-theoretic specialization), not a restriction of the Bunyakovsky statement itself, and it does not narrow or touch the single-polynomial primality question as worded in the frozen bullet. No AI system was mentioned in connection with the Yoon preprint, the Schinzel-H work, or any other source found; the 2026 AI-discovered counterexample events I encountered while searching (e.g. the Jacobian Conjecture counterexample found with the aid of a language model) concern an unrelated problem and have no bearing here.
competing_reading: One could argue the Yoon preprint should be coded 'claimed' on the theory that any standing, undisputed public proof claim of a major conjecture counts as 'claimed' regardless of venue prestige, since the rubric's 'claimed' bar is only a preprint or announcement not yet digested, not a peer-reviewed one. Against this: the DEEP_DIVE.md rubric's `claimed` category presumes a claim serious enough to attract eventual expert attention; this one has attracted none in over two years, appears formulaic/unreviewed similar to other undiscussed 'proof of X conjecture' preprints periodically posted to TechRxiv, and the Wikipedia/Grokipedia record of the field's consensus flatly contradicts it having succeeded. I judge 'open'/no_change_found is the better reading, but flag this as a genuine judgment call.
what_would_settle_it: Any expert commentary, arXiv posting, citation, or discussion thread engaging with the Yoon preprint's actual argument (confirming or refuting it) would settle whether it merits 'claimed' status; absent that, its total lack of uptake after two years supports treating it as noise.
